summary.en: The layout foundation is a mobile-first 12-column grid of containers, rows, columns and fixed gutters. Fixed containers keep a controlled width that suits reading; fluid containers span the full viewport for headers, footers and media-heavy areas. Breakpoints change grid behaviour at 576, 768, 992, 1200 and 1600px. Twelve columns divide in many ways, so even, asymmetric and single-column layouts are possible; keep text lines at roughly 60 to 80 characters, since they grow wide on large screens.

The grid follows the classic structure of container, row, column and gutter. The container centres content within a breakpoint-dependent width, rows group columns horizontally, columns carry content, and the fixed gutter comes from the horizontal padding of the column elements.

Two container variants exist. Fixed containers use defined maximum widths tied to the breakpoints and suit content areas that need a controlled width, while fluid containers stretch across the whole viewport and fit headers, footers or media-heavy areas.

The grid is mobile-first, so layouts are designed from small to large viewports and behaviour can change at defined thresholds. The column prefixes run from --kern-col-* below 576px through --kern-col-sm-*, -md-* (768px), -lg-* (992px), -xl-* (1200px) to --kern-col-xxl-* from 1600px.
The grid supports many layout variants, from simple single-column pages to complex multi-column structures, and the 12-column base makes widely different divisions easy to realise.
Shows even column layouts, where the 12-column base is divided into equal parts.
Shows asymmetric column layouts, where the 12-column base is divided into unequal parts.

Single-column layouts can produce very wide text blocks on larger screens, so keep line length in a comfortable range, ideally about 60 to 80 characters, and watch this at every breakpoint. Offsets let you create narrower columns and clearer reading structures on any device.
A mobile-first 12-column grid with container, row, column and fixed gutters; fixed containers limit reading width, fluid ones fill the viewport.

whenToUse.en: Use fixed containers where a controlled width helps readability, and fluid containers for headers, footers or media-heavy areas.

dos.en: Think layouts mobile-first, from small to large viewports, and let the grid change behaviour only at the defined breakpoints.
Keep the line length of text-heavy content at roughly 60 to 80 characters at every breakpoint.
Use column offsets when you need narrower columns and clearer reading structures.

donts.en: Do not let single-column layouts stretch text into overly wide blocks on large screens.
